audits.title: An audit of morphine prescribing in a hospice.

cycle1.result: 35% receiving morphine; deficiencies included omitted breakthrough doses, p.r.n.-only use for chronic pain, no review and no double night dose.

audits.other_findings: Prophylactic laxatives and anti-emetics were often not co-prescribed.
audits.citation: Neo SH, Loh EC, Koo WH. An audit of morphine prescribing in a hospice. Singapore Med J. 2001;42(9):417-419. PMID: 11811608.

audits.title: Oral morphine prescribing practices in severe cancer pain.
audits.standard: Locally set standards for adequacy of pain relief with oral morphine
audits.setting: Department of Pain and Palliative Care, St. John's Medical College Hospital, Bangalore (tertiary care)

cycle1.result: Only 50% achieved adequate pain relief; rescue dose given to only 20%.

audits.intervention: Education for doctors and nurses on starting, titrating and giving rescue doses of morphine, followed by circulation of local guidelines.

cycle2.result: 80% achieved adequate pain relief and 100% received rescue doses.

audits.other_findings: Twenty case files were analysed across the pre- and post-education audits. Failure to give regular and rescue doses caused inadequate pain relief.
audits.citation: B B. Oral morphine prescribing practices in severe cancer pain. Indian J Palliat Care. 2009;15(2):127-131. doi:10.4103/0973-1075.58458. PMID: 20668591.

audits.title: An audit of morphine prescribing in a specialist cancer hospital.
audits.standard: Palliative care unit recommendations for morphine prescribing
audits.setting: Specialist cancer hospital (Royal Marsden Hospital, London)

cycle1.result: Weaknesses included lack of breakthrough doses, prn oral morphine without regular oral morphine, and no guideline reference to co-prescription of aperients, antiemetics and night sedation

audits.intervention: Education programme targeting the identified deficiencies

cycle2.result: Some improvement in prescribing practice (no figures reported)

audits.other_findings: Persistent problems showed the need for an ongoing hospital-wide education programme.
audits.citation: Turner R, Clark J, Root T, McElligott L, Hardy J. An audit of morphine prescribing in a specialist cancer hospital. Palliat Med. 1994;8(1):5-10. doi:10.1177/026921639400800102. PMID: 7514071.

audits.title: ‘Spot’ audit of strong opioid prescribing at Musgrove park hospital, Taunton
audits.standard: Best practice and Trust policy: morphine first line (exceptions for renal impairment), PRN 1/6 of regular dose up to hourly, regular laxatives, antiemetic at least PRN
audits.setting: Musgrove Park Hospital, Taunton; 750-bed district general hospital, one day

cycle1.result: 100% adherence to Trust policy; morphine first line 68% (78% for hospital-started); 21% (6) no breakthrough analgesia; 65% met PRN standard; laxatives 48%; antiemetics 72%; 89% with renal impairment had appropriate second-line opioid.

audits.intervention: Practical prescribing guidance cards issued to junior doctors; re-audit planned in 1 year.
audits.other_findings: Only 4% (29/750) of inpatients were on regular strong opioids.
audits.citation: Michaels K, Jayaraman S, Lagan S. ‘Spot’ audit of strong opioid prescribing at Musgrove park hospital, Taunton. BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care. 2012;2(Suppl 1):A70.2-A70. doi:10.1136/bmjspcare-2012-000196.204.

audits.title: Prescribing of breakthrough opioid analgesia in acute hospitals – a multi site audit
audits.standard: National guidelines: breakthrough dose one sixth of total daily dose (target 90%), frequency hourly or two-hourly (100%), single dose not a range (100%)

cycle1.result: Poor prescribing practice varying significantly between trusts (figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Service improvement workshop for local teams, root-cause analysis, action plans and action learning sets for 1 year, then re-audit.
audits.other_findings: Earlier single-site pilot improved after a trust-wide plan and was maintained a year later; staff rotation was a barrier.
audits.citation: Wilkinson A, Alloway L. Prescribing of breakthrough opioid analgesia in acute hospitals – a multi site audit. BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care. 2012;2(Suppl 1):A74.3-A75. doi:10.1136/bmjspcare-2012-000196.217.

audits.title: AN AUDIT OF THE INITIATION, PRESCRIPTION AND ADMINISTRATION OF OPIOID ANALGESIA TO ADULT PALLIATIVE CANCER PATIENTS IN AN ACUTE HOSPITAL
audits.standard: NICE (2012) opioid guidance, NPSA (2010), NMC (2010) and local hospital standards; 15 standards
audits.setting: Acute hospital; adult palliative cancer patients

cycle1.result: Only a third of the 15 standards showed compliance (±10%); high rate of PRN-only prescribing, only 45 started on regular opioids.

audits.other_findings: Poor practice despite intensive education; recording explicit exceptions recommended.
audits.citation: Messam K, Cooper J. AN AUDIT OF THE INITIATION, PRESCRIPTION AND ADMINISTRATION OF OPIOID ANALGESIA TO ADULT PALLIATIVE CANCER PATIENTS IN AN ACUTE HOSPITAL. BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care. 2014;4(Suppl 1):A67.3-A68. doi:10.1136/bmjspcare-2014-000654.192.
